correctness.rationale: For every integer d,q>=3 the RK4 heat endpoint is a degree-four polynomial in the combinatorial Hamming Laplacian. The distance-regulated adjacency recursion yields exactly four nonzero offdiagonal shell types. The distance-three entry is h^3(1-h/h3) and becomes negative for all h>h3; distance-four entry is h^4. The diagonal is positive because the scalar degree-four exponential Taylor polynomial is positive for all nonnegative Laplacian eigenvalues. The displayed Bernstein-basis identities for distance-one and distance-two shell polynomials imply nonnegativity throughout [0,h3] for d>=4 and for d=3, q<=12. At d=3, q>=13, the last degree-three Bernstein coefficient (64-5q)/(81q) is negative; via t/(1-t) the cubic has exactly one positive root (Descartes), so the adjacent entry crosses once before h3. I independently reconstructed Hamming adjacency and Laplacian powers and checked at d,q=(3,12),(3,13),(4,3),(7,13): the distance-three entry vanishes exactly at h3, is negative just beyond, while distance-one at h3 changes from +1/4374 at (3,12) to -2/41067 at (3,13), as claimed. The all-parameter assertions rest on exact positive symbolic Bernstein coefficients, not finite tests. Row-sum one follows from L*1=0. Spectral stability alpha/(dq) > h3 follows from Laplacian eigenvalues jq and alpha>2.
